فِرِنْدٌ A sort of cloth, or garment, (Lth, T, O, K,) well known: (K:) an adventitious word, (Lth, T, O,) [from the Pers. پَرَنْد,] arabicized. (O, K.) ―
-b2- And [hence, app.,] فِرِنْدُ السَّيْفِ, (T, S, M, O, K,) and ↓ إِفْرِنْدُهُ , (S, O, K,) The diversified wavy marks, streaks, grain, or water, of the sword; syn. وَشْيُهُ, (T, S, M, O, K,) and جَوْهَرُهُ, (T, O, K,) and رُبَدُهُ [q. v.], (S, O,) and مَاؤُهُ الَّذِى يَجْرِى فِيهِ, (T, O, *) and طَرَائِقُهُ, (T, O,) i. e. سَفَاسِقُهُ. (T.) ―
-b3- And الفِرِنْدُ signifies The sword itself. (M, L, K.) ―
-b4- And The حَوْجَم; (K, TA;) i. e. (TA) the red rose. (M, TA.) ―
-b5- And The grains of the pomegranate. (AA, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
